Cognate with Scots you (“you”), Saterland Frisian jou (“you”), West Frisian jo (“you”), Low German jo, joe and oe (“you”), Dutch jou and u (“you”), German euch (“you”), Middle High German eu, iu (“you”, object pronoun), Latin vōs (“you”), Avestan 𐬬𐬋 (vō, “you”), Ashkun yë̃ (“you”), Kamkata-viri šo (“you”), Sanskrit यूयम् (yūyám, “you”).

senses.definition: the person or group of people being spoken or written to

examples.en: Can you help me with this heavy bag?
examples.vi: Bạn có thể giúp tôi với chiếc túi nặng này không?

examples.en: I hope to see both of you at the party.
examples.vi: Tôi hy vọng được gặp cả hai bạn tại bữa tiệc.

senses.definition: used to refer to anyone or people in general, not a specific person

examples.en: You have to work hard if you want to succeed.
examples.vi: Người ta phải làm việc chăm chỉ nếu muốn thành công.

examples.en: You never know what might happen tomorrow.
examples.vi: Người ta không bao giờ biết điều gì có thể xảy ra vào ngày mai.

senses.definition: used before a noun to speak directly to a particular group of people

examples.en: Do you two want to join us for dinner?
examples.vi: Hai bạn có muốn đi ăn tối cùng chúng tôi không?

examples.en: Be quiet, you children, and listen to the teacher.
examples.vi: Trật tự nào, các con, và hãy lắng nghe giáo viên.

senses.definition: used before a noun or adjective to emphasize strong anger, admiration, or other feelings

examples.en: You idiot, why did you leave the door open?
examples.vi: Đồ ngốc, sao bạn lại để cửa mở thế?

examples.en: You lucky girl, you won the first prize!
examples.vi: Đồ may mắn, cậu đã giành được giải nhất rồi!

The name of the Latin script letter U/u.

idioms.gloss: An affirmation of affection or deep caring, especially to a family member.
An expression of gratitude or politeness in response to something done or given.
An informal greeting, not requiring a literal response. In form a question, and thus followed by a question mark. Typical responses include
Asks the interlocutor whether or not they are able to speak in the English language.
Used to ask whether the interlocutor does or doesn't have a spouse.
Asks the age of the interlocutor.
Said to express greater gratitude than would be conveyed by thank you.
In which country or region were you born or raised?
Used to ask where the person lives.
Expresses discontent or contempt.
A phrase used at parting, and not necessarily implying that the person being addressed will be seen later by the speaker.
Asks the interlocutor for their identification
Used to ask what the interlocutor is currently doing.
A polite formula used when being introduced to somebody.
Said to someone who has just sneezed, as a polite remark.
Asks the interlocutor if they understand.
Said when handing something over to someone or doing a favour to them, usually to draw the recipient's attention to the exchange; equivalent to “thank you” when receiving something.
A request for help.
Expression of hatred, or intense disdain or dislike directed at someone.
May God bless you; said as a short prayer, benediction, or valediction for the recipient; usually religiously; sometimes nonliterally but rhetorically or culturally.
